Read the files of an export

Source: R/exports.R
soil_export_read.Rd

Reads the tables of an export back into R, typed as the synchronous reads type them: metadata.json is read first and drives the typing. The wide observations are typed as soil_observations() types them (fixed columns, markings and list columns; a variable column is numeric when wide_columns says so, <key>_n integer, a multi-value WoSIS cell gives the mean of its values in <key> and the values in <key>_values); the long observations as the long layout; the features as soil_features(). Values written as JSON text by the flat formats (CSV, TSV, GeoPackage: value_flags, cell_markings, profile_markings, components, ...) are parsed back to list columns. The result is a soil_table whose metadata has the shape of a synchronous read (with via_export, the job id, and export: format, content, layout, records, files, the variables of the selection), so soil_citations(), soil_revised_rules() and soil_columns() work on it.

Usage

soil_export_read(x, what = c("observations", "features", "metadata", "all"))

Arguments

x

A soil_export (downloaded), the path of an export zip, or the directory it was unzipped into. Client-side: not sent to the API.

what

"observations" (the default; for an export of content = "features" the features), "features", "metadata" (the parsed metadata.json) or "all" (a list features, observations, metadata). Client-side: not sent to the API.

Value

A soil_table (soil_layout "wide", "long" or "features"; an sf object for the features when sf is installed), the metadata list, or a list of them.

Details

Formats and packages: CSV, TSV and GeoJSON need no package; GeoPackage and Shapefile need sf. The features are an sf object (EPSG:4326) when sf is installed; without it the features of a CSV/TSV export keep their WKT in geometry_wkt and those of a GeoJSON export their GeoJSON in geometry_text. Shapefile fields are cut to 10 characters and 254 characters of text by the format: the known names are restored, the nested values stay text.

Empty fields of CSV and TSV are NA (the API writes null as an empty field). In the long layout value_raw of a CSV/TSV export is the JSON value of the cell text (a number when the text is a number).

No network, no right needed.

See also

Other exports: soil_export(), soil_export_from_error(), soil_export_status()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- soil_export(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", country = "KEN", format = "csv")
obs <- soil_export_read(x)
soil_columns(obs)
f <- soil_export_read(x, "features")
soil_export_read("exports/exp_20261019_101500_1a2b3c4d.zip", "metadata")$records
} # }
